data.title: Coal tar + Ketoconazole scalp lotion/shampoo
data.summary: I Antifungals — Other · Combination: keratoplastic/antiproliferative tar + imidazole antifungal
data.body:
_Topicals · I Antifungals — Other_

**Class:** Combination: keratoplastic/antiproliferative tar + imidazole antifungal

## Mechanism of action
- Coal tar: antiproliferative (activates aryl hydrocarbon receptor → normalises keratinocyte differentiation), antipruritic, anti-inflammatory
- Ketoconazole: reduces Malassezia load
- Together they treat scaling, inflammation and the yeast driver in scalp disease

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Seborrhoeic dermatitis and dandruff of scalp, especially thick scaling
- Scalp psoriasis (mild) and sebopsoriasis

## Dose & formulations
- Lotion: apply to scalp at night, wash next morning (or as directed) 2–3 times weekly
- Shampoo: lather, leave 3–5 min, rinse; 2–3 times weekly, then weekly for maintenance

## Adverse effects
- Tar: odour, staining of hair (especially grey/blonde) and fabrics, folliculitis, irritation, photosensitivity
- Ketoconazole: irritation, dry hair

## Contraindications
- Acutely inflamed or broken scalp skin; infected scalp
- Avoid tar in pustular or erythrodermic psoriasis

## Pregnancy & lactation
Coal tar: avoid in pregnancy (theoretical carcinogenicity); ketoconazole topical safe.

## Viva points
- Tar = AhR agonist (normalises differentiation), ketoconazole = anti-Malassezia
- Tar shampoos may stain grey hair yellow

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.51 (Therapeutic shampoos) and ch.57 (Miscellaneous topicals — tar); Khopkar ch.28. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
